children: Shares of JSW Steel Ltd., Tata Steel Ltd. and other steel-linked stocks are expected to be in focus in trade on Friday, September 18, after domestic brokerage firm Motilal Oswal said steel prices remained firm in the second quarter of FY27 despite seasonal weakness in demand.

According to the brokerage, lean channel inventories, maintenance-led supply constraints and rising input costs have supported domestic steel prices, with prices recovering across both flat and long products.

Domestic hot-rolled coil (HRC) prices rose 7% month-on-month to a four-year high of ₹62,000 per tonne in September 2026, while cold-rolled coil (CRC) prices increased 8% month-on-month to ₹70,500 per tonne.
Rebar prices have also recovered sharply to ₹56,800 per tonne in September from ₹48,850 per tonne in June 2026.
Motilal Oswal said the improvement in steel prices has been driven largely by cost pass-through, as higher input costs have raised the cost base for steelmakers.
Premium Australian coking coal prices have increased to around $300 per tonne from $260 per tonne in June, while iron ore and pellet prices have also remained firm.
Despite seasonal weakness, domestic steel volumes have remained fundamentally healthy, according to the brokerage.
Between April and August 2026, India's finished steel production increased 3.7% year-on-year (YoY) to 67.4 million tonnes (mt), while finished steel consumption grew 7.2% YoY to 70.3 mt.

However, global steel market trends remained less supportive. Global crude steel production declined 0.6% YoY to around 1.08 billion tonnes during January-July 2026, while China's output fell 3.1% YoY to around 577 mt.

Motilal Oswal remains constructive on domestic steel pricing and expects the sector to enter the second half of FY27 with a stronger realisation environment if post-monsoon demand normalises as expected.
The brokerage said this could result in steel realisations being considerably stronger than current consensus assumptions.
Among its top picks in the sector, Motilal Oswal has a price target of ₹1,340 for JSW Steel and ₹220 for Tata Steel.

title: Motilal Oswal sees stronger steel prices in H2FY27; check out its top stock picks
